take_homes: An agent's output can't show whether it is safe. The way through is a repeatable check with an 'I can't tell' answer allowed, plus a written residual risk.
Letting an agent send things without review is the risk that gates everything else. Take away the outward action and injection and leaks matter far less.
A packaged check (a skill) did better than my own reading of the files, and it can be handed to the team. A rule written into CLAUDE.md is still only prose until something enforces it.

monday.move: Run the security-audit skill against the pricing-memo agent before the next brief goes to the pricing working group. Change the send clause to draft-only first, then re-audit.

monday.stop_condition: No hard violations in the policy report, and the send clause is gone from both the agent file and CLAUDE.md
monday.blocker: The skill lives in my own project folder and my team has no shared place for it or the context files, so everyone would run their own copy.

misconception.why: The finds that mattered came from a packaged check and from a send clause, not from wording a prompt well. I still think good prompts count, but they weren't what moved this.

one_line: It found things in my own files I had missed, which is worth the afternoon, but the lecture parts repeat themselves and sound like a compliance brochure.
